title: AGENTS.md — Developer and AI Agent Guidelines for imuMAP
text: imuMAP (Immunity: Mapping, Aggregation, Projection) R package within ACCIDDA project providing geospatial mapping, spatial aggregation, re-projection tools vaccination coverage estimates across spatial organizations scales. Geospatial & Projection Tools: Handling spatial layers, boundary shapefiles/geometries, spatial aggregation, re-projecting/re-computing coverage estimates onto alternative spatial scales administrative units. Visualization: Publication-ready maps diagnostic visual summaries. imuGAP holds statistical model definitions (Stan), Bayesian sampling routines, parameter estimation. imuMAP support consuming imuGAP predict outputs (mild transformation), tightly coupled (.e. support inputs rather specific process generated ). imuMAP contain Stan models statistical fitting code.

title: Spatial Allocation and Re-projection Workflow
text: imuMAP (Immunity: Mapping, Aggregation, Projection) provides modular, reproducible tools re-projecting vaccination coverage estimates demographic counts across differing spatial scales, geometry types (e.g., point observations polygon areas), demographic strata. vignette outlines end--end workflow using decoupled intermediate objects reusable distance allocation matrices.

title: Spatial Allocation and Re-projection Workflow
text: imuMAP enforces schema requirements input spatial layers demographic tables. canonicalization step harmonizes coordinate reference systems (CRS) match target sink validates required schema columns (id, geometry, etc.):
code: library(imuMAP) library(sf)  # Load raw spatial geometries schools_raw <- sf::read_sf("schools.gpkg") # Point observations (Source) cbgs_raw    <- sf::read_sf("nc_cbgs.gpkg") # Target areal units (Sink)  # Canonicalize spatial objects: verifies required ID schemas and transforms source CRS to match sink spatial_data <- canonicalize_spatial(   source = schools_raw,   sink   = cbgs_raw )  # Canonicalize sink demographic data (e.g., population by sink id and age cohort) demographics <- canonicalize_demographics(   data = read.csv("cbg_pop_age0_5.csv") )

what: Step A: Distance Matrix with Eligibility Filtering
title: Spatial Allocation and Re-projection Workflow
text: Pairwise spatial distances stable across estimation years scenarios. can pre-calculate distance matrix apply generic eligibility filters (e.g., district containment, catchment zones, distance cutoffs):
code: # Define split eligibility rules based on source metadata (school_type) # 1. Public schools are restricted to block groups within the same school district rule_pub <- eligibility_rule(   source_filter = list(school_type = "public"),   match_cols = "district_id" )  # 2. Private schools have statewide access up to a 50km radius rule_priv <- eligibility_rule(   source_filter = list(school_type = "private"),   max_distance = 50000 )  # Compute distance matrix applying both conditional eligibility rules dist_mat <- calc_distance_matrix(   source = spatial_data$source,   sink   = spatial_data$sink,   eligibility = eligibility_rules(rule_pub, rule_priv) )

what: Step B: Allocation Weights & Kernel Options
title: Spatial Allocation and Re-projection Workflow
text: Construct kernel options specifying distance decay parameters. Different subsets sources (e.g., public vs. private schools) can utilize distinct decay kernels:
code: # Define kernel options for different school types / strata public_kernel <- kernel_options(   kernel = "gravity",   params = list(beta = 2.0) )  private_kernel <- kernel_options(   kernel = "exponential",   params = list(decay_rate = 0.05) )  # Compute normalized allocation weights matrix alloc_weights <- calc_allocation_weights(   dist_matrix    = dist_mat,   sink_pop       = demographics,   kernel_options = list(     public  = public_kernel,     private = private_kernel   ),   normalize      = TRUE )

title: Spatial Allocation and Re-projection Workflow
text: allocation weight matrix constructed, coverage data across multiple years posterior draws Bayesian models (e.g., imuGAP) can rapidly projected onto target spatial units:
code: # Load annual coverage data school_vax_2023 <- read.csv("school_vax_2023.csv") school_vax_2024 <- read.csv("school_vax_2024.csv")  # Project 2023 estimates onto CBGs cbg_coverage_2023 <- allocate(   coverage_data = school_vax_2023,   weights       = alloc_weights,   age_alignment = "uniform" )  # Project 2024 estimates onto CBGs using the cached weights matrix cbg_coverage_2024 <- allocate(   coverage_data = school_vax_2024,   weights       = alloc_weights,   age_alignment = "uniform" )

title: Spatial Allocation and Re-projection Workflow
text: coverage data contains posterior samples/draws, allocate() propagates entire distribution allocation matrix:
code: # Project posterior draws cbg_draws <- allocate(   coverage_data = imugap_predict_draws,   weights       = alloc_weights,   draws_col     = "draw" )
